sections.html:
Chesterfield County lies directly south of Richmond, with the James River along much of its northern edge and the Appomattox River along much of its southern one. The county seat is Chesterfield Court House, and there are no incorporated towns. The 2020 census counted 364,548 residents, the fourth most populous county in Virginia, and the county's 2025 estimate is 397,148. It covers 437 square miles.

Postwar commuter growth built much of the county, which means many houses are decades old. Tired roofs, older HVAC systems and dated kitchens often keep a listing from selling, and a lender-backed buyer may demand repairs that a cash buyer will not.

Communities include Chester, Midlothian, Bon Air, Brandermill, Ettrick, Bermuda Hundred and Matoaca, and the northern part is often called North Chesterfield. Ettrick lies in Chesterfield but is mostly served by a Petersburg mailing address. A seller there should ask the county tax office, not rely on the postal city, to learn which locality bills the parcel.

Chesterfield reassesses real estate every year. Notices are mailed by February 1 and show values as of January 1. The county says assessments must reflect 100 percent of fair market value, based on inspections, sales data and comparisons with similar nearby properties.

The Board of Supervisors sets the tax rate. The county lists $0.89 per $100 of assessed value for 2026.

StepDate
Values set as ofJanuary 1
Assessment notices mailedBy February 1
File with Real Estate AssessmentsMarch 15
File with the Board of EqualizationApril 15

Two filings, in order: Real Estate Assessments by March 15, then the Board of Equalization by April 15. Late applications are not processed, and you cannot skip the first level.

  1. Review your values on the county's READ site or contact the office.
  2. Get the application and file a separate one for each property.
  3. Attach support: up to three comparable properties, a recent appraisal or photos, and for income property three years of income and expense statements plus a current rent roll.
  4. If a representative files for you, add a notarized Letter of Authorization.
  5. An appraiser may ask questions or inspect, then notifies you of the outcome.

State code makes the Board of Equalization independent: a Circuit Court judge names its members and the state tax department trains them. Under 58.1-3379, the assessor's value is presumed correct and the owner must rebut it. Real Estate Assessments is at 6801 Mimms Loop, phone 804-748-1321, email assessor@chesterfield.gov.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Chesterfield's current bill is due Monday, December 7, 2026, with a 10 percent penalty for missing it. Virginia's 58.1-3916 caps interest at 10 percent a year and the property penalty at 10 percent.

The Treasurer's Office is at 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832, with mail to P.O. Box 70. The phone is 804-748-1201, and hours are weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • Online through the Citizen Portal, which requires an account.
  • By phone at 855-933-5661, around the clock.
  • Through your bank's bill pay, mailed to P.O. Box 70.
  • At payment kiosks in seven county library and administration locations, which take cash, cards and checks around the clock.
  • By drop box at the Lane B. Ramsey Administration Building, checks or money orders only.

Processor fees are 2 percent for credit cards and a flat $2.50 for debit cards. An eCheck has no fee.

The county's Automated Payment Service is free. Taxes are debited on the due date after about 30 to 45 days of activation, and a returned payment carries a $50 fee on top of any bank fees. The Citizen Portal shows invoices for the most recent six years, which helps an heir cleaning up an old account. The Treasurer can explain anything older.

Ask the closing agent whether your parcel sits in a special district. The Real Estate Assessments page names a contact for the Lower Magnolia Green Community Development Authority, and a district can add a charge beyond the normal county bill.

sections.h2: Selling with the tax bill behind
sections.html:
If you cannot pay on time, the county takes payment plan applications. Staff reply within two business days, approval is not guaranteed, and interest and fees continue to build while the plan runs. A plan also does not release a DMV stop, which is lifted only when accounts are paid in full. That matters if you owe both vehicle and real estate tax.

At closing, Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 under 58.1-802. Interest grows daily, so request a payoff figure for your actual closing date.

sections.h2: Steps to sell a Chesterfield house
sections.html:
Start from the assessment notice that lands by February 1. Compare the January 1 value with what you expect a buyer to pay, and decide by March 15 whether it is worth a first-level appeal. If you are inside the window, gather your support: up to three comparable properties, a recent appraisal or photos.

Next, check who bills the parcel. Confirm the locality with the county tax office, especially if your mailing address is Petersburg or another city. Then ask the Treasurer for a payoff dated to your closing and look at the Citizen Portal for the past six years of invoices.

The title company settles the open tax from your proceeds, collects the seller's grantor tax and records the deed. If the house needs work, put a listing's repairs and showings next to a direct as-is offer and count the cost of waiting.

A short call can save a closing delay. Ask what is paid and what is open for the current year. Ask for the payoff on your expected closing date, because interest grows daily. Ask whether any older year is unpaid, and whether a DMV stop is in place on a vehicle in your name. Ask which payment method clears fastest if you are paying just before closing: the phone line and the eCheck option work any hour, and the kiosks take cash, cards and checks.

Write down the answers, note the name of the person who gave them, and send everything to your closing agent the same day so the settlement statement matches what the county expects to collect.

With more than 364,000 residents, Chesterfield has plenty of owners who inherit a house or have moved away and manage it from far off while tax statements keep arriving. Get the Treasurer's current balance early, read the county's payment plan page before the next due date, and use the Citizen Portal to see recent billing.

Cash Home Buyers can buy a Chesterfield County house as is, including one with back tax or repairs, and the payoff comes out of the proceeds at closing. Call or text the address for a written offer.

faqs.q: What rate applies to Chesterfield real estate in 2026?
faqs.a: $0.89 per $100 of assessed value, as set by the Board of Supervisors.

faqs.q: What are the Chesterfield appeal deadlines?
faqs.a: March 15 with Real Estate Assessments and April 15 with the Board of Equalization. Late applications are not processed.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Chesterfield Treasurer?
faqs.a: Go to 9901 Lori Road, Room 101, Chesterfield, VA 23832, weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., or call 804-748-1201.

faqs.q: Does a Chesterfield payment plan stop penalties?
faqs.a: No. Interest and fees keep accruing during a plan, and a plan does not release a DMV stop.

faqs.q: Is selling with back taxes possible in Chesterfield?
faqs.a: Yes. Your proceeds normally pay the balance at closing, so get a payoff figure from the Treasurer first.
